finding.observed: ClerkTokenVerifier constructed PyJWKClient with cache_keys=true, adding a per-signing-key LRU with no time-based expiration above the finite JWKS-set cache. WebSocket auth also called verifier.verify synchronously from the async terminal handler, so a JWKS fetch could block that event loop path.
finding.product_contract: Clerk key rotation must remain observable and network-backed verification must not synchronously block the canonical WebSocket PTY event loop.

primary_dependency_evidence.pyjwt_contract: PyJWKClient finite JWKS-set cache defaults to 300 seconds; cache_keys=true adds a separate LRU signing-key cache without time-based expiration; timeout is configurable.
primary_dependency_evidence.clerk_contract: Clerk supports networkless public-key verification or JWKS-backed verification; real key-rotation behavior remains an external acceptance gate.

bounded_execution.interpretation: The network admission failure is not a product test failure. This receipt supports the exact clerk_auth constructor mechanism and source-bound terminal offload line only; it is not exact full-head or live Clerk/browser/PTY runtime evidence.
